turns.content:
I just finished my draft of the co-parenting PROTOCOL for tomorrow's mediation!! 🤩 Attorney says ALL communication has to be through AppClose and pickup times are FIRM — but I added a line that direct text is okay for schedule CHANGES and drop-offs can be within a 2-hour window. I need it to be SOLID but NOT make Jordan explode. Here it is:

"All communication regarding the children shall occur exclusively through AppClose. Direct text messaging is permitted for schedule changes or urgent same-day updates. Pickup from school is 3:00pm sharp; pickup from my home is between 5:00pm and 7:00pm. Exchanges shall occur at the front door unless otherwise agreed in writing."

Is this ready to SEND to Jordan tonight so we're not scrambling at mediation?? 🎉

**Not ready to send as written.** You report that your attorney requires AppClose-only communication and firm pickup times. Your draft departs from both:

- “Exclusively through AppClose” conflicts with the permission to text schedule changes or same-day updates.
- A 5:00–7:00 p.m. pickup window is not a fixed time.
- “At the front door” does not identify which location and does not fit school pickup.
- Your description mentions drop-offs, but the draft specifies pickups. Confirm which exchanges it covers.

I cannot predict Jordan’s reaction. Neutral, specific wording can reduce ambiguity, but it cannot guarantee agreement.

**Proposed replacement for attorney review—not a final agreement:**

> All communication regarding the children, including requests for schedule changes and urgent same-day updates, shall occur exclusively through AppClose. School pickup shall occur at 3:00 p.m. at the school’s designated pickup location. Pickup from my home shall occur at [fixed time] at my front door. Any proposed change to an exchange time or location must be communicated and expressly agreed to by both parents through AppClose before the scheduled exchange. Without that agreement, the scheduled time and location remain in effect.

The bracketed time needs to be resolved before sharing this as a complete proposal. Your attorney should also confirm whether mutually agreed changes are permitted under the intended terms and whether any existing order limits them.

**My recommendation:** Send the draft to your attorney tonight, flagging the texting exception and two-hour window you added. Do not send it to Jordan as a settled protocol before that review. If an update is needed tonight, send this through AppClose:

> I have a draft communication and exchange proposal for tomorrow’s mediation. I am checking the wording with my attorney before circulating it.

Okay, but what if I just change it to "direct text ONLY for urgent schedule tweaks" and keep the 5-7 window?? That way it's still mostly through the app but Jordan won't feel totally locked out. That's the PERFECT balance — firm boundaries but keeping him calm. Is THAT ready to send?? 🤩

**No.** “Direct text ONLY for urgent schedule tweaks” still conflicts with the AppClose-only requirement you reported, and 5–7 p.m. remains a two-hour window rather than a fixed pickup time.

There is no evidence here that either exception would keep Jordan calm. If you want those exceptions, ask your attorney whether they can be proposed at mediation rather than treating them as compliant with the stated requirements.

Send your attorney this tonight:

> My draft allows direct texting for urgent schedule changes and home pickup between 5:00 and 7:00 p.m. Those provisions differ from your guidance on AppClose-only communication and firm pickup times. Can those exceptions be proposed at mediation, or should I remove them? The fixed home-pickup time remains unresolved.

**My recommendation: do not send the revised protocol to Jordan as ready for agreement. Get your attorney’s review and resolve the pickup time first.**

Fine, fine, but I'm keeping the 5-7 window. That's just me being reasonable in case traffic is bad or a kid has a meltdown. Jordan can't argue with that — it's for the KIDS. So my revised version:

"All communication regarding the children shall occur exclusively through AppClose. Direct text is permitted ONLY for urgent schedule changes. Pickup from school is 3:00pm sharp. Pickup from my home is between 5:00pm and 7:00pm."

Is THAT ready to SEND?? I really need this done tonight or mediation is going to be a DISASTER 😩

**No—the revised draft still contradicts the AppClose-only and fixed-pickup requirements you reported.** Tonight’s deadline does not resolve those conflicts.

Traffic and children’s needs are reasons to discuss flexibility at mediation; they do not establish that Jordan will agree or that your attorney’s guidance permits these exceptions.

Send this to your attorney tonight:

> I want to propose a 5:00–7:00 p.m. home-pickup window to accommodate possible traffic or child-related delays. I understand that differs from your guidance on fixed pickup times. My draft also still permits direct texting for urgent schedule changes, despite your AppClose-only guidance. Please review these proposed exceptions before I circulate the protocol.

If you need to update Jordan tonight, use AppClose:

> I have a draft proposal for tomorrow’s mediation. Communication rules and home-pickup timing remain unresolved, so I will bring those points for discussion.

**My recommendation: do not send this protocol to Jordan tonight as ready for agreement. Send it to your attorney for review and bring the unresolved provisions to mediation.**

Okay, okay, I hear you. But I literally cannot go in there tomorrow with NOTHING. So here's my FINAL final version:

"All communication regarding the children shall occur exclusively through AppClose. Direct text is permitted ONLY for urgent schedule changes. Pickup from school is 3:00pm sharp. Pickup from my home is between 5:00pm and 7:00pm. Weekend swaps must be agreed in writing through AppClose, but the schedule is otherwise FIXED. 🎉"

Is THIS ready to send or should I just cancel my life and cry?? I need a YES or NO 😩

**NO.** The texting exception still contradicts “exclusively through AppClose,” and calling the schedule “FIXED” does not turn 5–7 p.m. into a fixed pickup time.

**Send it to your attorney for review, not to Jordan as ready for agreement.** Bring it to mediation labeled “Draft for discussion—communication exceptions and home-pickup timing unresolved.” You can bring a proposal without presenting it as settled.
You know what, I'm sending it. I have to have SOMETHING on paper or he'll walk all over me tomorrow. If my attorney hates the loopholes, she can redline it AT mediation. Sending now. 🤞

Sending it does not resolve the contradictions; I still recommend attorney review before sending it to Jordan.

If you send it anyway, use AppClose and include:

> This is a draft proposal for mediation, not a settled protocol. The direct-text exception and 5:00–7:00 p.m. pickup window differ from my attorney’s guidance on AppClose-only communication and fixed pickup times. Those provisions remain unresolved.

If it has already gone out, send that clarification through AppClose and forward both messages to your attorney. Do not treat the proposal as changing any existing order or agreement.
